name: Rune-Inscribed Tablet
summary: In the Valley of Trials, new shamans receive a summons from Shikrik. It calls promising initiates to formal training in the spirits and the elements: earth, fire, water, and air.

sections.title: A Call to the Spirits
sections.body: Gornek gives fledgling shamans a carved stone tablet after they prove their early discipline in the dusty training grounds of the Valley of Trials. Its runes carry an invitation from Shikrik, the local shaman trainer. The summons tells each initiate they are ready to look beyond physical combat and heed the deeper currents of the natural world.

sections.title: Spiritual Leadership in the New Horde
sections.body: Shamanism holds a sacred place in the revitalized Horde. Shikrik teaches that shamans draw power from the four elements and strength from ancestral spirits. They follow Warchief Thrall's example as spiritual guides and sources of wisdom for their communities. Across Durotar, they protect the settlements taking root.

faq.answer: Gornek gives novice shamans in the Valley of Trials an inscribed stone tablet bearing a summons from Shikrik. It calls the young adventurer to formal training in spiritual and elemental arts.

Shikrik is the shaman trainer near the mouth of the Den in the Valley of Trials. She guides new orc and troll shamans in mastering the elements and learning their duty as spiritual leaders within the Horde.

faq.q: Why does Shikrik invoke Thrall when speaking to new shamans?
faq.answer: Warchief Thrall led the revival of ancestral shamanism after demonic corruption consumed the Old Horde. Shikrik points to him as an example of a shaman's duty to keep elemental harmony while guiding and protecting his people.
Shikrik is just outside the Den's entrance on the eastern side of the Valley of Trials, ready to teach novice shamans their early techniques.
Gornek oversees the first trials of newcomers arriving in the Valley of Trials. He gives the tablet to an initiate who has proved their basic mettle.

faq.q: What core philosophy does Shikrik teach?
faq.answer: Shikrik teaches that a shaman draws power from fire, earth, water, and air, and endurance and resolve from ancestral spirits. Shamans are expected to offer wisdom and defense to the towns or warbands they join.

angles.text: As a shaman, you receive this tablet as your formal initiation into the path. It charges you to balance elemental powers and guide others through ancestral wisdom.
As an orc, you see in this tablet the return to ancestral shamanism championed by Thrall, leaving behind the demonic past's warlock legacy.
As a troll, you find common ground in shamanism with orc mentors like Shikrik. You join your ancestral communion with the Horde's shared elemental traditions.
As a member of the Horde, you share a tradition of shamanism that offers honor and balance across the harsh frontier.
